correctness.rationale: Exact inversion gives \((1-w)^w=1+\log(1-u/p)\). With \(t=\log(1-w)\), this becomes \(t e^t-t=\kappa(u)\). On \(t<0\), \(t(e^t-1)\) decreases continuously from \(+\infty\) to zero, proving existence and uniqueness of the admissible branch. Back-substitution yields both quantile formulas; the embedded checker confirms direct substitution.

value.rationale: Quantiles are used in the target paper for simulation, percentile inference, and quantile-based shape summaries. The result turns a model-specific nonlinear root equation into an established special-function evaluation, proves the admissible branch is unique, and gives a genuine function of u for the focal FExKw model. It is a structural inversion rather than a numerical recomputation.
